title: March of Dimes concert at Municipal Auditorium: applause for Roosevelt's picture
summary: Funny story of the band taking bows while the audience applauded Roosevelt's portrait behind them.

This is the funniest story ever. See this? Uh-huh. We played that, I noticed the other day somehow that was the anniversary of F.R.'s birthday, it was the anniversary of F.R.'s birthday, it was the year that he first started with the March of Dimes. Uh-huh. It was the first time. So we had a big concert down at the Municipal Auditorium. This is the Municipal Auditorium, the stage, the bandstand and everything up here, and they had an American flag up there and Roosevelt's picture on it. And when we got finished, it was not there except until after the finale. Now the band is facing this way, and you can't tell what the hell's in vacuum.

So the people applauded, and just about when they stopped applauding, they started applauding again. So Lou Forbes comes out, and he's taking a bow, and he's telling you guys, come on outside and take a bow. We stand about a footwork, taking a bow. But they don't know that they're not clapping for us, they're clapping for Roosevelt's picture, the American flag, that's in back of us. This is a funny story. This is from 1933.
